title: Friday's page
how: Two looks and one decision. Tap any picture to open it full-screen at its full resolution: pinch to zoom, swipe to the next, Close to come back. One tap each; a note is optional. Your picks save on the page.
foot: Anything you do not pick carries onto the next page.

sections.name: The street, stage 1: wet, worn, the far end climbing round a bend. Carry on this way?
sections.note: Short of the Hook sheet and KCD2, said first (I do not recommend yes on the look): the pavements still read as glossy tiles, warmer than the sheet's grey stone; the road's cracks repeat everywhere and it reads drier than the sheet's; the sky has no cloud shapes; the hill is stacked boxes with blob trees; Mickey's window is black; the cars and people are stand-ins; litter shows as white slivers; at night a test pattern shows in the empty shop's window (a bug).
sections.detail: WHAT IT IS: the street from the game's own camera and exposure, at 2560 by 1440. The far end climbs one in twelve and curves away round a bend, the houses stepping up with it; the distance hazes the way the research found studios do it. The road and the flags are wet with the sky's sheen. Every wall is worn by rule, from a generator: streaks under every sill, splash at the foot of every wall and gable, the gables weathered, algae at the downpipes, soot at the stacks, oil where cars stand, puddles with soft wet rims. At night the lamps make pools with darkness between them (9 to 11 stops from pool to gap). FOUND TODAY: every wear mark had been drawn wrongly since it was added (turned a quarter, and printing the packs' preview pictures, lit spheres, instead of their stain masks); fixed, which is why the walls now show wear. A fresh reviewer who had not seen it said no for a 2026 game; the faults above are theirs and mine. The sky's clouds were set aside after two tries; the next direction is known. WHAT YOUR YES MEANS: the method carries on into stage 2 (the ground surfaces, the hill, the far end), not that this frame is finished.

sections.name: Rita's, the pawnbroker: one shop window made the new way. Make the other eleven like it?
sections.detail: WHERE IT FALLS SHORT OF THE HOOK SHEET AND KCD2 (said first, as your rule asks; I do not recommend yes): the display is sparser than a real pawnbroker's, which was crammed with gold; the room and the velvet are cleaner and more evenly lit than a real shop; the street in the glass is a soft reflection, never a sharp one; the room is softer than the goods in front of it, so its wall notices cannot be read. WHAT IT IS: a room behind the glass that shows depth as you walk past (a picture projected the way games do it, the floor kept clear because anything standing on it smeared), a real display on a velvet bed (ring trays, watches, cameras, clocks, vases, priced tickets, two notices against the glass), glass that now reflects the street (it had shown none: Unreal's see-through glass was dimming its own reflection), and at night the window lit, its white light falling on the pavement and the road beside the orange lamps. The first fresh reviewer failed an earlier cut (the floor pieces smeared; no reflection); a second passed all ten of its checks, with the notes above. The other windows are still the old flat pictures; they are made only after your yes, about half a day each. The cars, skip and pallets in these frames are the next item.

sections.name: The parked cars: take them off the street for the friends' build (recommended), or build them properly now (3 to 5 days)?
sections.note: Your ruling was real 1990 things or removed. The research (production/research/period-vehicles-and-props) puts a car that passes the bar at 3 to 5 days by script, then 1 to 2 days for each other kind; the phone box, skip and pallets about 3 days together, all by script with nothing bought and no sign-in. I recommend the cars off the street for the friends' build and the phone box, skip and pallets made now; the cars come back after the build. Part of their crudeness was a fault, fixed today: they were drawing a quarter of their own triangles.
